sections.h2: The Coconut Creek market in Broward County
sections.html:
Coconut Creek had an estimated 58,626 residents in mid-2025, up from 52,909 in 2010 and 57,833 in 2020. Owner-occupied homes had a typical value of $309,600 over 2020 through 2024. Owners occupy 64.8% of the housing. Rent at the midpoint is $2,102 a month, so owners of rental units can set that income against what a sale would bring.

Check whether your home belongs to a homeowner or condominium association. Its rules can add steps to a sale, and the vacation rental affidavit on the city's site refers to notice to a mandatory association.

The city's vacation rental page says its regulations do not prohibit vacation rentals or limit how long or how often a home is rented. They exist to protect neighborhoods and life safety, and every vacation rental must register and obtain a Vacation Rental Certification.

If you hold one, tell buyers up front. The certification counts toward what a rental earns, and a buyer who wants one must file a fresh application. The city lists these details:

  • Application or registration fee: $250. Renewal: $250. Re-inspection: $40.
  • Registrations expire annually and must be renewed before September 30.
  • Fire safety and code compliance inspections come before the first certificate, under Ordinance No. 2021-003, by appointment.
  • Packet items: a Florida DBPR transient public lodging license, Florida Department of Revenue sales tax registration, a Broward County business tax receipt and Broward tourist development tax registration.

The city also offers a notarized-letter option for owners whose booking sites collect taxes. Ask the city's business tax office for the current form.

sections.h2: Landlords: what to do before selling a rented house
sections.html:
Start with the lease. Ending a tenancy that renews monthly requires notice of at least 30 days. When rent is late, the tenant gets 3 days of written notice, and weekends and court holidays do not count. The state's eviction statute lays out the notice and the court steps, so follow them if a tenant must leave before closing.

If the tenant stays through the sale, the rent keeps flowing and no gap opens between occupants. Put the lease, the security deposit amount and the rent ledger in the contract package.

sections.h2: Broward deed tax and recording fees
sections.html:
Deeds in Broward pay the same 70 cents per $100 of price charged across the state, with Miami-Dade the lone exception. The base includes any mortgage or encumbrance, assumed by the buyer or not. The Broward clerk collects at recording, and the state can pursue every person on the deed whatever the contract says.

Recording is billed separately by statute, at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each page after, with other per-page fees added. Ask the closing agent to list every one.

Every parcel is assessed as of January 1. To receive a homestead exemption of up to $50,000, apply by March 1 and show the home was your permanent residence on January 1. The first $25,000 reaches every tax. The second $25,000 applies only above $50,000 of value and only to non-school taxes.

Under Save Our Homes, assessed value grows each year by 3 percent or inflation, whichever is less. A sale sends the parcel back to just value the following January 1. November brings the bills, with a discount starting at 4 percent and shrinking to 1 percent by February. April 1 marks delinquency. A mid-year closing means the title company splits the tax with the buyer.

Foreclosure here is a court matter. The clerk runs the auction 20 to 35 days after final judgment, or later with the lender's consent, and a sale before then pays the lender out of proceeds. An inherited house may qualify for summary administration if the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or if the death was more than two years ago.

Either case rewards an early call to the servicer, a Florida attorney or the probate clerk. A cash buyer can work around those dates, yet the court sets the schedule.

sections.h2: What if property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquency starts April 1. The tax collector then sells certificates on the unpaid bills by June 1, and bidders offer the lowest interest rate they will accept, in quarter-point steps. The holder cannot demand payment from the owner until two years after April 1 of the issue year.

After that, the holder may apply for a tax deed, paying a $75 fee, and the clerk runs the auction. A homestead's opening bid includes half of its assessed value. Back taxes come out of closing proceeds, so ask the title company for the payoff figure.

sections.h2: Florida tax breaks that may apply
sections.html:
Where a local ordinance allows it, owners 65 or older with household income under the limit may receive an extra homestead exemption of up to $50,000. A 10 percent or greater disability, with an honorable discharge and Florida residency, brings a $5,000 cut in assessed value. A total and permanent service-connected disability may earn a full homestead exemption.

Homestead ends when you rent the home or move out, though a servicemember may rent without losing it. Ask the Broward property appraiser which exemptions sit on your parcel before closing.

Once you have a contract, plan the handoff. Schedule your move for a day or two before closing so the house can be cleaned and photographed empty. Arrange to end service on trash, internet and any lawn or pool care, and notify the association if you have one. Ask the title agent exactly when funds will be released, and keep a copy of the signed deed and settlement statement for your records. If you sold a rental, give the tenant's contact and deposit details to the buyer in writing so nothing is lost in the transfer.

sections.h2: Before a quick Coconut Creek closing
sections.html: Quick sales still need paperwork. Open permits and code violations can delay a closing, so ask the Building Division and the code office about your address. If you have an association, contact it early, because approvals can run longer than a buyer expects. Pull together your deed, latest tax bill and payoff letters. Weighing cash against a listing? Take commission, repairs and holding costs off the listing number and choose whichever result suits your deadline. Before signing day, review the title agent's draft settlement statement line by line.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Coconut Creek house that has a vacation rental certification?
faqs.a: Yes. The certification belongs to the current owner, and a buyer planning short-term stays has to register separately. Check the city's annual September 30 renewal date and your fee status before closing.

faqs.q: Do I owe the city anything before I sell my Coconut Creek home?
faqs.a: Call the Building Division about open permits and the code office about open violations, since both can hold up closing.

faqs.q: How quickly can a cash sale close here?
faqs.a: Usually faster than a listing, because no lender or appraisal is involved. HOA approval, title work and lien payoffs can still add days.

faqs.q: Who pays Broward deed tax on a sale in Coconut Creek?
faqs.a: The state holds every person on the deed liable, and contracts typically assign it to the seller. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration.

faqs.q: What happens to my Coconut Creek tenant if the house sells?
faqs.a: The lease generally carries on unless it ends or the proper notice is served. A tenant renewing monthly is owed at least 30 days of notice.
